newsitem.title: USA: US court denies Chevron equity suit at Elk Hills.
newsitem.headline: US court denies Chevron equity suit at Elk Hills.

text.p: A U.S. District Court in California has rejected Chevron Corp's claim that its share of shallow oil zone at Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve be redetermined.
The U.S. District Court of Eastern California said Chevron, which has a stake in the U.S. government oil field, did not "have a clear and certain claim for relief."

Chevron had claimed that the U.S. Energy Department should get a redetermination of the shallow oil zone wells, figuring a reassessment of the California oil field would show the company's share should increase about 4 percent.
The court said the deadline for redetermining the shallow oil zone had validly been extended to May 10, and said the Energy Department had not shown "bad faith" in the issue.
The court also said the Energy Department has indicated it will make a decision in April, and said: "Whatever harm Chevron is suffering (if any) will cease shortly."
The department is in the process of trying to sell the Elk Hills reserve.
